problems.title: Warehouse Rank Gateway
problems.story: Warehouse Rank Gateway is an independent Quadrantcode practice scenario. A planning team has reduced its observations to an integer sequence and needs a precise first valid sorted position result before the next decision can be made.
problems.statement: Implement the required function for Warehouse Rank Gateway. Interpret the supplied sequence exactly as described in the input contract, compute the first valid sorted position, and return only the requested integer. The function must handle boundary cases and the largest stated input without modifying any external state.
problems.inputFormat: values[0] is the query target. values[1..] is a nondecreasing sorted sequence.
problems.outputFormat: Return the zero-based position inside the sorted sequence where target first could appear.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: The complete integer encoding described by this problem.

constraints: values[1..] is sorted in nondecreasing order
The answer may equal the sequence length.

examples.explanation: Example 1 follows the stated first valid sorted position process. Every contributing value is visible in the input, and the computed result is 2.
Example 2 follows the stated first valid sorted position process. Every contributing value is visible in the input, and the computed result is 2.

testCases.explanation: Applying the first valid sorted position rule to this input produces the stated result without using any unstated data.
Applying the first valid sorted position rule to this input produces the stated result without using any unstated data.

hints: Maintain a half-open search interval [low, high).
When the middle value is at least the target, keep the middle position in the candidate interval.

editorial.overview: Binary search for the first element that is not smaller than the target, using the sequence after the first input cell.
editorial.bruteForceApproach: Scan from the beginning until an element is at least the target.
editorial.optimalApproach: Repeatedly halve a half-open interval. Move high to mid when the middle is large enough; otherwise move low past mid.
editorial.correctnessProof: All indices below low are known smaller than target and every valid answer remains below high. Each update preserves these invariants and shrinks the interval. At low = high, that index is the first possible insertion position.

problems.title: Skyline Banner Area
problems.story: Skyline Banner Area is an independent Quadrantcode practice scenario. A planning team has reduced its observations to an integer sequence and needs a precise largest contiguous rectangle result before the next decision can be made.
problems.statement: Implement the required function for Skyline Banner Area. Interpret the supplied sequence exactly as described in the input contract, compute the largest contiguous rectangle, and return only the requested integer. The function must handle boundary cases and the largest stated input without modifying any external state.
problems.inputFormat: The array values contains nonnegative bar heights in left-to-right order.
problems.outputFormat: Return the greatest rectangular area supported by consecutive bars.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: The complete integer encoding described by this problem.

constraints: The result fits in a signed 64-bit integer.

examples.explanation: Example 1 follows the stated largest contiguous rectangle process. Every contributing value is visible in the input, and the computed result is 10.
Example 2 follows the stated largest contiguous rectangle process. Every contributing value is visible in the input, and the computed result is 4.

testCases.explanation: Applying the largest contiguous rectangle rule to this input produces the stated result without using any unstated data.
Applying the largest contiguous rectangle rule to this input produces the stated result without using any unstated data.

hints: A bar can extend until the first smaller bar on each side.
Use a monotonic increasing stack and finalize taller bars when a shorter bar arrives.

editorial.overview: Use a monotonic stack of starting positions and heights. Each pop finalizes the widest rectangle for that height.
editorial.bruteForceApproach: Choose every left boundary, extend right, maintain the minimum height, and evaluate each rectangle.
editorial.optimalApproach: Keep increasing heights with their earliest valid starts. A lower height closes all taller rectangles; a zero sentinel closes the rest.
editorial.correctnessProof: A popped height cannot extend through the current lower bar, and its stored start is the earliest position it can reach. Thus the computed width is maximal for that height. Every height is eventually popped, so the best rectangle is considered.

c11.functionSignature: long long solve(const long long *values, int n)

serialization.input: Whitespace-separated signed integers read into values.

c11.referenceSolution: long long solve(const long long*v,int n){long long best=0,*h=malloc(sizeof(long long)*(n+1));int*s=malloc(sizeof(int)*(n+1)),top=0;for(int i=0;i<=n;i++){long long x=i<n?v[i]:0;int start=i;while(top&&h[top-1]>x){top--;if(h[top]*(i-s[top])>best)best=h[top]*(i-s[top]);start=s[top];}if(!top||h[top-1]<x){h[top]=x;s[top++]=start;}}free(h);free(s);return best;}

cpp17.functionSignature: long long solve(const vector<long long>& values)

serialization.input: Whitespace-separated signed integers read into values.

cpp17.referenceSolution: long long solve(const vector<long long>&v){vector<pair<int,long long>>st;long long b=0;for(int i=0;i<=(int)v.size();i++){long long h=i<(int)v.size()?v[i]:0;int s=i;while(!st.empty()&&st.back().second>h){auto p=st.back();st.pop_back();b=max(b,p.second*(i-p.first));s=p.first;}if(st.empty()||st.back().second<h)st.push_back({s,h});}return b;}

serialization.input: Whitespace-separated signed integers read into values.

java.referenceSolution: static long solve(long[]v){int n=v.length,top=0;long[]h=new long[n+1];int[]s=new int[n+1];long best=0;for(int i=0;i<=n;i++){long x=i<n?v[i]:0;int start=i;while(top>0&&h[top-1]>x){top--;best=Math.max(best,h[top]*(i-s[top]));start=s[top];}if(top==0||h[top-1]<x){h[top]=x;s[top++]=start;}}return best;}

serialization.input: Whitespace-separated signed integers read into values.
Whitespace-separated signed integers read into values.

javascript.referenceSolution: function solve(v){const st=[];let b=0;for(let i=0;i<=v.length;i++){const h=i<v.length?v[i]:0;let s=i;while(st.length&&st.at(-1)[1]>h){const p=st.pop();b=Math.max(b,p[1]*(i-p[0]));s=p[0];}if(!st.length||st.at(-1)[1]<h)st.push([s,h]);}return b;}

hints: A bar can extend until the first smaller bar on each side.
Use a monotonic increasing stack and finalize taller bars when a shorter bar arrives.

editorial.overview: Use a monotonic stack of starting positions and heights. Each pop finalizes the widest rectangle for that height.
editorial.bruteForceApproach: Choose every left boundary, extend right, maintain the minimum height, and evaluate each rectangle.
editorial.optimalApproach: Keep increasing heights with their earliest valid starts. A lower height closes all taller rectangles; a zero sentinel closes the rest.
editorial.correctnessProof: A popped height cannot extend through the current lower bar, and its stored start is the earliest position it can reach. Thus the computed width is maximal for that height. Every height is eventually popped, so the best rectangle is considered.

c11.functionSignature: long long solve(const long long *values, int n)

serialization.input: Whitespace-separated signed integers read into values.

c11.referenceSolution: long long solve(const long long*v,int n){long long best=0,*h=malloc(sizeof(long long)*(n+1));int*s=malloc(sizeof(int)*(n+1)),top=0;for(int i=0;i<=n;i++){long long x=i<n?v[i]:0;int start=i;while(top&&h[top-1]>x){top--;if(h[top]*(i-s[top])>best)best=h[top]*(i-s[top]);start=s[top];}if(!top||h[top-1]<x){h[top]=x;s[top++]=start;}}free(h);free(s);return best;}

cpp17.functionSignature: long long solve(const vector<long long>& values)

serialization.input: Whitespace-separated signed integers read into values.

cpp17.referenceSolution: long long solve(const vector<long long>&v){vector<pair<int,long long>>st;long long b=0;for(int i=0;i<=(int)v.size();i++){long long h=i<(int)v.size()?v[i]:0;int s=i;while(!st.empty()&&st.back().second>h){auto p=st.back();st.pop_back();b=max(b,p.second*(i-p.first));s=p.first;}if(st.empty()||st.back().second<h)st.push_back({s,h});}return b;}
